## Part II — mmacos / pymacos function catalog

Each entry shows the MATLAB (mmacos) and Python (pymacos) form of the same operation where both exist; both wrap the same engine routine in `macos_api_mod.F90`, so arguments, units and behavior match.  An entry with only one language is a coverage gap in the other (noted).

### Session, prescription and model I/O

#### Session

- **mmacos:** `classdef Session < handle`
- **pymacos:** *not available*

OO veneer over the +macos function package.  m = macos.Session(model_size) initializes the engine and returns a handle.  Every method delegates to the same-named +macos package function -- the only state in the class is the loaded Rx path (cached so it's discoverable via m.rx_path).

<!-- BEGIN NOTES fn-Session -->
<!-- END NOTES fn-Session -->

#### cbm

- **mmacos:** `c = macos.cbm()`
- **pymacos:** *not available*

Base-units-to-metres conversion factor (CBM). c = macos.cbm() returns the SI-metres value of one BaseUnit in the currently loaded Rx (e.g. 1e-3 for an Rx in mm).  Used internally when callers want to feed/read distances in SI metres while the prescription is in its native units.

<!-- BEGIN NOTES fn-cbm -->
<!-- END NOTES fn-cbm -->

#### has_rx

- **mmacos:** `tf = macos.has_rx()`
- **pymacos:** `pymacos.has_rx()`

True iff a prescription is loaded. Detects via `num_elt > 0`; if init hasn't run yet, mmacos errors internally and we return false.

<!-- BEGIN NOTES fn-has-rx -->
<!-- END NOTES fn-has-rx -->

#### init

- **mmacos:** `macos.init(model_size)`
- **pymacos:** `pymacos.init(model_size)`
- **engine API:** `macos_api_mod::init`

Initialize / resize the macos engine. macos.init(MODEL_SIZE) allocates the engine for prescriptions up to MODEL_SIZE elements / rays / etc.  Must be called once per MATLAB session before any other macos.* call.  See also: macos.load_rx, macos.has_rx.

<!-- BEGIN NOTES fn-init -->
<!-- END NOTES fn-init -->

#### load_rx

- **mmacos:** `nElt = macos.load_rx(rx_path)`
- **pymacos:** `pymacos.load(macos_rx)`
- **engine API:** `macos_api_mod::load_rx`

Load a prescription file (.in) into the macos engine. N = macos.load_rx(RX_PATH) loads the prescription at RX_PATH and returns the number of elements N (>0).  RX_PATH may be supplied with or without the trailing '.in' — macos's OLD command appends '.in' unconditionally, so we strip a trailing '.in' if present (otherwise macos tries to open 'foo.in.in').

<!-- BEGIN NOTES fn-load-rx -->
<!-- END NOTES fn-load-rx -->

#### modify

- **mmacos:** `macos.modify()`
- **pymacos:** `pymacos.modify()`

Reset ray-trace-dependent state (the SMACOS MODIFY cmd). Call after any direct prescription mutation (perturb, set_elt_*) before re-running a trace, so cached intermediates don't carry stale geometry.

<!-- END NOTES fn-modify -->

#### compose

- **mmacos:** `I = macos.compose(srf, wavelengths, npix, dx, opts)`
- **pymacos:** `pymacos.compose(srf, wavelengths, npix, dx, dx_unit)`

Multi-wavelength PSF on a fixed pixel grid (COMPOSE+ADD). I = macos.compose(SRF, WAVELENGTHS, NPIX, DX) assembles a composite image at element SRF: for each wavelength in WAVELENGTHS the source wavelength is set, the field is propagated to SRF, and its intensity is accumulated onto a single NPIX x NPIX detector grid of pitch DX. The result is the INCOHERENT sum -- a broadband PSF.

#### gs_zernike_segment_basis

- **mmacos:** `[B, mask, info] = macos.gs_zernike_segment_basis(session, rx_path, opts)`
- **pymacos:** *not available*

Gram-Schmidt-orthonormalized Zernike basis over a segment's TRUE (irregular) aperture -- a grid-poke influence basis that respects the segment shape.  Circular Zernikes cross-talk on a hex / edge segment; manufacturers spec figure over the segment aperture, so the modes are orthonormalized over that aperture (MGS).

#### m2v

- **mmacos:** `[vec, jndx] = macos.m2v(mat, indx)`
- **pymacos:** *not available*

Vectorise a 2D OPD matrix preserving non-zero index map. [vec, indx] = macos.m2v(mat)   first call -- find non-zeros + cache. vec        = macos.m2v(mat, indx)  reuse cached index struct.  indx is a struct with fields: .i      Nnz×1 row indices of non-zero positions

Read per-ray data from the most recent trace. r = macos.get_ray_info(N) returns a struct with fields: .pos       3×N double  — intersection position with current surface .dir       3×N double  — incoming direction at that surface .opl       N×1 double  — cumulative OPL from source .ok_trace  N×1 logical — true if the ray traced successfully

- **pymacos:** *not available*

Per-category ray-status codes after the most recent trace. r = macos.get_ray_status(N) returns a struct with fields: .status      N×1 int32 — per-ray RayStat_* code: 0 = OK, 1 = Obscured, 2 = Miss, 3 = Bracket, 4 = MaxIter, 5 = Undef .fail_elt    N×1 int32 — element index where failure was first
